offering_description.value: Energy Recovery designs and manufactures equipment that recovers pressure energy in reverse-osmosis desalination and industrial wastewater treatment systems. It sells to plant builders, equipment manufacturers and operators, and supplies aftermarket parts and equipment services. It has also developed pressure exchangers for commercial refrigeration systems that use carbon dioxide.

primary_products.value: Pressure exchangers for reverse osmosis; hydraulic turbochargers; centrifugal pumps; replacement parts; carbon dioxide refrigeration pressure exchangers

primary_services.value: Equipment commissioning; maintenance and repair; equipment refurbishment

customer_segment.value: B2B: Desalination plant contractors, water treatment equipment manufacturers, industrial plant operators and refrigeration equipment manufacturers; B2G: Public water utilities that operate desalination plants

end_markets.value: Seawater desalination; industrial wastewater treatment and reuse; commercial refrigeration

revenue_model.value: product sales: Pressure exchangers, pumps, turbochargers and replacement parts; service fees: Equipment commissioning, maintenance and refurbishment

value_chain_position.value: OEM / manufacturer: Turns ceramic and metal components into pressure recovery equipment for plant builders, system manufacturers and operators; service provider: Services installed pressure recovery equipment for plant operators

geography_served.value: global: North America, Latin America, Europe, the Middle East, Africa and Asia

specialization.value: related lines: Pressure recovery devices and pumps for water treatment, plus pressure exchangers for refrigeration

distribution_channels.value: direct sales: Project sales to plant contractors and aftermarket sales to plant operators; partners / resellers: Equipment manufacturers that integrate pressure recovery devices into their systems

regulatory_exposure.value: medium: High-pressure equipment is subject to applicable pressure equipment and industrial safety standards.

notes: The current commercial status of the carbon dioxide refrigeration line is uncertain.
